newsitem.title: UK: Mideast clean tankers quiet but trend seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Mideast clean tankers quiet but trend seen firm.

text.p: The clean tanker market was relatively quiet in the Middle East due to Ramadan and in Asia because of the Chinese new year, while rates generally softened in the West due to low enquiry levels, brokers said.
But E.A. Gibson Shipbrokers said in a weekly report that "the underlying trends for the second half of February are still looking healthy."

They said that although the Mediterranean market was quieter this week than recently, "there is not an over-abundance of tonnage and, with an expected increase in orders, it can be assumed that the current slide in freights will be halted and possibly reversed."
Brokers Galbraith's said clean tonnage was scarce in the Continent and the Med for February dates, with 60,000 tonnes from both commanding over W200.
Although naphtha rates in the Med held steady to firm, gas oil fell sharply to W230 for 30,000 tonnes and down as far as W200 for vessels with a less suitable last cargo history, Gibson said.
East of Suez, rates were expected to fall during the holiday period, after 55,000 tonnes Singapore/Japan was reported to have been fixed at W205, down 7.5 points, they added.

Galbraith's said that although a sharp fall in rates for 30,000 tonners to India was not likely, there were "a number of weaker vessels that will gradually pull the rates down across the board" in Asia.
On a more positive note, brokers said there was reasonable demand for unleaded gasoline moving transatlantic, even though this was on a smaller scale than in early January.
Brokers said Caribbean rates has softened on lower activity, though Boston beam vessels were relatively strong at W295 for 29,000 tonnes, against W280 for other ships.
"Present interest should, however, ensure that these rates are maintained," Gibson said.
The U.K./cont sector was steady, with 25,000 tonne cargoes at about W210. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
